title: FeasibilityEnvelope
description: Operator + Professor's joint declaration of what the harness ACTUALLY has access to at production-entry time, before any claim is designed. This anchors strong+safe claim construction: a 'deployment-grade' claim cannot be promised if the matching resource (real data, live LLM, compute budget) is not in the envelope. Validators reject mismatches at design_initial_claim_contract and revise_root_after_reject time.

data_sources_available.description: What data the harness can actually read for this thread. Each entry is either an adapter_id registered under settings.json.data_adapters (real data path) or the literal string 'synthetic' (the harness can generate). 'synthetic' alone forbids deployment-scope claims.

scope_note.description: Brief description of what this data covers — date range, universe, asset class, etc.

llm_oracles_available.description: What LLM oracles are reachable: 'subscription_claude_code' (Claude Code interactive driving the thread itself, free), 'live_anthropic_api' (paid, requires billing_ack), 'deterministic_proxy' (no LLM, deterministic substitute), or 'none'. Live API entries require operator ack flags in settings.

compute_budget.description: Practical compute envelope. The Professor uses these to scope claims that fit — e.g., a 19,200-measurement experiment may need to be chunked.

baseline_provenance_available.description: Baselines that exist with verifiable paper / arxiv / repo provenance via the market_research dossier. self-made baselines are NOT listed here.

provenance.description: arxiv id, doi, repo url, or reference_papers/ filename

operator_intent.description: What kind of outcome the operator is willing to accept as 'goal achieved'. target = preferred; acceptable_alternative_scopes = fallback options before the system gives up scope-wise (it never gives up the user-goal+AC-accept dual-gate, but it may settle for narrower deploy-grade than 'deployment' if real data is missing).
